page: Microsoft Azure E96s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V, running on x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, providing 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for tile and int8 operations, and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core). It includes no bundled local storage, relying on external Premium Storage, and contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded execution and high memory subsystem throughput. In stress-ng, multi-core throughput reaches 95,011.59 (top 25%), paired with a PassMark CPU score of 97,473.82 and Geekbench multi-core score of 21,854.0 (both in the top 10%). Large-block uncached memory operations deliver 509.22 GB/sec read bandwidth and 209.25 GB/sec write bandwidth, positioning memory throughput in the top 10%. Highly parallelized tasks show substantial capacity, reflected by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 605.28 GB/sec and Clang compilation benchmark at 61,908.0. For database and in-memory scenarios, Redis SET operations achieve 137.56 million operations/sec and PassMark database operations register 36,143.23.

Instruction set support enables competitive CPU-based machine learning inference despite lacking GPUs. Leveraging Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, prompt processing achieves 3,346.39 tokens/sec on 135M models and 41.06 tokens/sec on 70B parameter models (top 10%). Single-thread processing remains standard, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 1,950.59 and Geekbench single-core at 2,152.0.

Without local temporary disks, all persistence depends on remote storage solutions. Azure E96s_v6 suits memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large in-memory databases like Redis or SAP HANA, enterprise relational databases, large-scale Clang build pipelines, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E96s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs and 48 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Supported by 768.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per vCPU) and a 260 MB L3 cache, it delivers top-tier memory bandwidth reaching 509.22 GB/sec read and 209.25 GB/sec write on large blocks. The instance incorporates Intel AMX and AVX-512 vector acceleration, driving high throughput in multi-core metrics like PassMark CPU (97,473.82), Clang compilation (61,908.0), and Redis operations (137.56 million ops/sec). The configuration contains no discrete GPUs and provides no local ephemeral storage, utilizing network-attached Premium Storage instead. Azure E96s_v6 is suited for large-footprint in-memory caches, enterprise database servers, high-density compilation pipelines, and CPU-based LLM inference.
